purpose: Prepare interns to frame, build, evaluate, secure, document, deploy, and defend AI systems responsibly under human oversight.
global_rules: All work must remain within authorized labs, VMs, accounts, networks, datasets, and equipment.
Never expose private/client data, credentials, secrets, or production identifiers to unapproved tools or submissions.
Prefer synthetic, anonymized, or properly approved public data and record provenance and licence.
AI output must be independently verified; consequential decisions require qualified human review.
Students must disclose AI assistance and document errors, limitations, troubleshooting, and time honestly.
Supervisor approval is required before production changes, external communications, paid resources, shared accounts, security testing, or real-world deployment.

days.objective: Confirm the approved workstation and create a responsible-AI readiness record.
learning_outcomes: Explain AI Orientation and Responsible Use in clear professional language and connect it to an authorized AI workflow.
Use Python, Jupyter, VS Code to complete the day objective safely.
Produce and independently verify evidence for: Confirm the approved workstation and create a responsible-AI readiness record.
Apply Beyond safety, privacy, ethics, human-oversight, and documentation standards.
practical_procedure: Review Day 0 prerequisites and read the complete Day 1 objective before changing the lab.
Prepare only the authorized workstation, VM, account, dataset, or sandbox; capture the approved starting state.
Create the folder Day_001_ai_orientation_and_responsible_use with evidence, src or notebooks, output, and report subfolders as relevant.
Complete the practical objective: Confirm the approved workstation and create a responsible-AI readiness record.
Record tool versions, inputs, assumptions, commands or code, expected output, observed output, and any deviations.
Verify the result independently by rerunning from a clean state, checking a second measurement/test, or obtaining recorded peer review.
Perform the relevant privacy, bias, security, licensing, and human-oversight checks before accepting the result.
Package the required evidence and write a concise professional technical report with an AI-assistance disclosure.
safety_ethics_and_beyond_lab_rules: Use only synthetic, anonymized, public, or supervisor-approved data; never upload private or client data to an unapproved AI service.
Keep passwords, tokens, API keys, personal records, and production identifiers out of code, prompts, notebooks, screenshots, and reports.
Work only in authorized labs, VMs, accounts, networks, datasets, and equipment; obtain supervisor approval before any production or shared-account change.
Treat AI/model output as unverified until checked against code, metrics, approved sources, or qualified human review.
Disclose AI assistance, licences, limitations, failed attempts, and troubleshooting honestly; keep time entries truthful.
